query: Which bibliometric normalization methods best compare AI-in-finance subfields across years and disciplines (FWCI, citation percentiles, field-normalized citations)?

response.query: Which bibliometric normalization methods best compare AI-in-finance subfields across years and disciplines (FWCI, citation percentiles, field-normalized citations)?
response.answer: Field-weighted Citation Impact (FWCI) and citation percentiles are best for comparing AI-in-finance subfields across years and disciplines. FWCI normalizes citations by field, while percentiles rank citations within a field. Both methods provide reliable cross-disciplinary comparisons.

results.title: Scopus metrics
results.content: # Scopus Metrics. Scopus metrics are a comprehensive, trustworthy and transparent way to demonstrate your journal, article, author and institutional influence. Subscribe to Scopus and access metrics. ## Journal-level metrics. **Four Scopus-specific metrics** can be found on **a document’s metrics details page**: total number of citations by a date range of the user’s choosing, citations per year for a range, citation benchmarking (percentile) and Field-weighted Citation Impact. PlumX Metrics: Also found on a document’s metrics details page, **five comprehensive, item-level metrics** that provide insights into the ways people interact with individual pieces of research output (articles, conference proceedings, book chapters, and many more) in the online environment. Learn more about CiteScore metrics, a suite of eight metrics that tell a richer story about research and researcher influence. ## View Scopus metrics for free.
